content_metadata.description: The video follows John Robinson, the founder of 'Our Ability', as he reflects on his journey from struggling with unemployment to creating a platform that empowers people with disabilities. Through interviews and real-world projects, the video's narrative showcases how 'Our Ability' bridges the gap between education and employment for individuals with disabilities, highlighting collaboration with universities and corporations.

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: I decided to go to Syracuse University and study television radio film management.
Four of us were in the communication school with the same GPA, same internship, same professors,
and they got jobs immediately and did not get my first job offer until four and a half
years later.
And in the back of my mind, I never forgotten the unemployment in my life.
I asked myself, what do I really want to do?
Our ability is an answer to that question.
We want to lower the unemployment rate for people with disabilities and we can help build
the dreams of people with disabilities all over the country.
About two years ago, I sat down with our Thomas at the high school and said, I have an idea.
A lot of our work is in experiential kind of practice and I consult is that practice
to enable students to see how that works.
When he said, we've got the partnerships with Microsoft and we have the student base that
wants to learn, we can help you pull the thread through.
They get clients, they get real problems to work with and then they put in students
to solve the problems.
This gives you a way to refine how you react to the triggers in a real world situation
and apply what you've learned in class.
Consulting with a client actually makes you learn a lot of things that are industry-related
and not curriculum-related.
We're working with Microsoft to do a better interface to engage people with disabilities
at their point of contact and right now today we're made a testing voice to text that
is Azure-driven.
Our primary responsibility is to work on the chatbot.
AI gives us an amazing opportunity to engage through chatbot, voice to text, text to voice,
in a more rapid, more engaging way.
And so what connect is today is it's an ability system.
So people with disabilities tell us who they are, tell us their work experience and
businesses that we work with today can reach out and employ.
With AI and machine learning we're going to revolutionize the way people with disabilities
find work.
If we're giving a chance and we have the right adaptive equipment we can do just about
anything.
I think our ability will allow us to connect with other organizations easier and have them
more open-minded.
We know that with all the Microsoft products that are dealing with accessibility and artificial
intelligence there is going to be some fantastic inventions that are going to allow us to continue
to draw up the skills and ability of people with disabilities around the world.
We can't wait for them all.
AI hoisted the customers.
When you determine you can do anything and I'm living proof.

youtube_description:
Syracuse’s School of Information Studies (iSchool) collaborated with Our Ability, empowering students to help create an AI-powered job search interface for people with disabilities.

The iSchool partners with businesses and government to drive experiential learning for students while building AI solutions with Microsoft technology that help solve real-world problems, such as the solution from Our Ability that helps people with disabilities gain employment.

Learn about Our Ability: https://www.ourability.com/

Learn more on Microsoft's Education blog: https://educationblog.microsoft.com/en-us/2020/03/new-report-shows-big-opportunities-to-transform-higher-education-through-ai/

**********************************

The Syracuse University School of Information Studies is preparing the next generation of information professionals for exciting, high-demand, well-paid careers. The iSchool offers a wide range online and on-campus degree programs in the fields of Library Science, Information Management & Technology, Enterprise Data Systems, and Applied Data Science. Explore to see if the iSchool is right for you.  

https://ischool.syr.edu/academics/overview/
